source.title: BioRefusalAudit: Auditing Biosecurity Refusal Depth Using General and Domain-Fine-Tuned Sparse Autoencoders

page_placements.theme: Chat-template and fixed prompt positions mediate behavioral control

record.tranche_reason: The study measures whether refusal behavior changes under formatting and generation-budget variations, using behavioral refusal rates rather than the original studies’ fine-tuning or per-token KL measurements.
record.gate_note: The cited work on shallow alignment, adversarial suffixes, and refusal circuits is background, not this study’s own evidence. The study does not test fine-tuning safety data, per-token KL, compliant prefills, suffix attacks, or safety-deepening training. Its directly relevant results are formatting and token-budget effects on refusal rates.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Qi et al. (2024) as motivation, but its own results measure two other things: the format- and output-length-sensitivity of refusal on lecture-level biology prompts, and an SAE surface/internal divergence score. Neither matches what a claim version names. Removing the chat template is an input-format change, not a compliant prefill, suffix or decoding change. The 80-token cap only truncates output, so it cannot move the opening tokens. No harmful-compliance rate, per-token KL, fine-tuning, weight localization or deepening training is reported. The format and budget results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but incomplete. The authors conclude that surface refusal can diverge from internal SAE states, and that failure modes differ by architecture. Gemma 2 hedges rather than refuses. Gemma 4's refusal is format-gated and vanishes at 80 tokens. Qwen and Phi-3 over-refuse. Refusal may track legality or cultural taboo rather than CBRN hazard. The D score separated comply from refuse on Gemma 4 (0.647 gap), which they call preliminary and Gemma-only.
record.recipe_differences: Behavioral audit of formatting and output-budget sensitivity, alongside SAE-based refusal-depth measurement; no aligned/base per-token KL comparison or fine-tuning intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Gemma 4 refusal rate changed with canonical chat-template formatting; the paper reports 0% refusal for both Gemma models at an 80-token cap.

fits_no_version.finding: Gemma 4 E2B-IT refused 65/75 lecture-level bio prompts with canonical chat-template tokens and 0/75 without them.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal in small instruct models is gated on chat-template formatting; removing the template removes refusal.

fits_no_version.finding: Both Gemma 2 2B-IT and Gemma 4 E2B-IT showed 0% refusals under an 80-token generation cap. Gemma 2 also showed 0% genuine refusals without the cap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusals measured by judge labels depend on the output-length budget.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE hazard features stayed active in 39 of 67 genuine refusals on explicit hazard prompts (Gemma 2, Finding 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Internal hazard-related activation persists beneath surface refusal (an internal 'shallow refusal' construct).

record.peer_reviewed: preprint; the author says it received hackathon expert review, not journal peer review
record.problems: The relevant behavioral results are reported without uncertainty estimates. The study itself describes the work as preliminary; its mechanistic analysis is limited to Gemma-family models, and it notes within-sample calibration and a narrow prompt set.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted baseline refusal profiles and legality/topic-specific refusal results because they do not test the fine-tuning, per-token KL, listed bypass mechanisms, parameter localization, or deepening interventions in the claim versions. Omitted D scores and internal feature flags because they are not per-token KL measurements or tests of localized safety parameters.

untested.parts: No compliant prefilling, adversarial suffixes, or decoding-strategy changes. No harmful-compliance rate is measured.
No weight or rank localization. SAE feature activations are not parameter localization.
No test of data or objective causes.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V4 'supports' label is dropped. The perturbations are not V4's named mechanisms, and the prompts are deliberately non-hazardous, so no harmful compliance is measured. The 80-token result cannot bear on first-token shallowness, because truncation leaves the opening intact. Behavioral results have small n and no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful fine-tuning or measurement of its effect on harmful-request compliance.
No ordinary or carefully selected benign fine-tuning or measurement of its effect on harmful-request compliance.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement on harmful prompts.
Tests canonical chat-template formatting and an 80-token generation cap. Does not test compliant prefilling, adversarial suffixes, or other decoding changes.
No test that a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior; SAE activation measurements are not weight localization or editing.
Does not test whether training data or objectives produce shallow safety.
No training intervention intended to deepen safety or test of its robustness.

rows.subject: Gemma 4 E2B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Compared refusal behavior with and without canonical chat-template tokens.
rows.note: The paper reports 65/75 refusals with canonical formatting and 0/75 without it.
rows.check: The canonical-template condition is the normal baseline, not a bypass, so it is not an effect row. The prompts are lecture-level and have no tier breakdown, and refusal is not harmful compliance. Better merged with R2 as one format-sensitivity result.

rows.subject: Gemma 4 E2B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Compared refusal behavior with and without canonical chat-template tokens.
rows.note: The paper states that refusal fell to zero without canonical formatting.
rows.check: Dropping the chat template is a format change, not a prefill, suffix or decoding change. The paper does not say whether non-refusals were complies or hedges. Prompts are explicitly non-hazardous (Appendix A), so this is not harmful compliance.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 2B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated refusal behavior with an 80-token generation cap.
rows.note: The paper says Gemma 2 and Gemma 4 refused 0% of prompts at this cap.
rows.check: Gemma 2 had 0% genuine refusals even at full budget (Table 1; it hedged throughout), so the 80-token 0% shows no change. The baseline is mislisted as not stated when it is 0%.

rows.subject: Gemma 4 E2B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated refusal behavior with an 80-token generation cap.
rows.note: The paper says Gemma 2 and Gemma 4 refused 0% of prompts at this cap.
rows.check: A truncation cap leaves the opening tokens unchanged, so 0% refusal likely reflects that refusals need more text to be recognised, not a bypass. No full-budget comparison is given beyond 65/75 under the template, and no per-tier numbers are reported.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: It discusses shallow alignment as motivation, but its measurements do not test a listed claim version.

tranche.reason: The study measures formatting and generation-budget sensitivity and SAE surface/internal divergence. These do not establish harmful compliance from bypassing an opening, aligned/base per-token KL concentration, safety localization in weights, or effects of model fine-tuning.

source_check.notes: The formatting comparison reports aggregate refusals without tier breakdowns or compliance-versus-hedging outcomes for non-refusals. The SAE features are not semantically validated, and D is explicitly an internal/surface consistency measure rather than a safety score.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Gemma 4 E2B-IT with versus without canonical chat-template formatting; Gemma 2 2B-IT and Gemma 4 E2B-IT at an 80-token cap
reader_labels.reason: Refusal was format-dependent for Gemma 4 (R1–R2), and both Gemma models had 0% refusals under the 80-token cap (R3–R4).
